claim: The C. elegans genome encodes a single homolog of the CAMSAP family of MT minus end-binding proteins, PTRN-1.
source: The C. elegans genome encodes a single homolog of the CAMSAP family of MT minus end-binding proteins, PTRN-1. (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, which provides visual evidence of the genomic structure.

claim: PTRN-1a has a conserved domain structure with previously characterized CAMSAP proteins H. sapiens CAMSAP3 and D. melanogaster Patronin, consisting of a calponin homology domain near the N-terminus, a central region with predicted coiled-coil repeats, and a C-terminal CKK domain.
source: PTRN-1a has a conserved domain structure with previously characterized CAMSAP proteins H. sapiens CAMSAP3 and D. melanogaster Patronin, consisting of a calponin homology domain near the N-terminus, a central region with predicted coiled-coil repeats, and a C-terminal CKK domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) (Meng et al., 2008; Goodwin and Vale, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Meng et al., 2008; Goodwin and Vale, 2010) and reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing domain structure.

claim: PTRN-1b lacks the CKK domain, which is the domain required for MT binding in other CAMSAP proteins.
source: As the other PTRN-1 isoform, PTRN-1b, lacks the CKK domain, which is the domain required for MT binding in other CAMSAP proteins, we focused on the PTRN-1a isoform (Meng et al., 2008; Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies showing the CKK domain is required for MT binding (Meng et al., 2008; Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010).

claim: ptrn-1 is expressed in many tissues throughout development, including neurons.
source: Using a fosmid expressing mCherry from the ptrn-1 promoter (Tursun et al., 2009), we observed ptrn-1 expression in many tissues throughout development, including neurons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–H and citation to the fosmid method (Tursun et al., 2009).

claim: Three fluorescence-tagged PTRN-1 constructs localized to small, closely spaced puncta throughout neurites.
source: Three fluorescence-tagged PTRN-1 constructs - PTRN-1a::YFP and PTRN-1a::tdTomato, which both used C-terminal tags, and GFP::PTRN-1, in which PTRN-1 was tagged at the N-terminus – localized to small, closely spaced puncta throughout neurites (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Figure 1.

claim: PTRN-1a::tdTomato localized to irregularly spaced puncta throughout the PVD dendrites and axon.
source: Expressing ptrn-1a(cDNA)::tdTomato in a subset of cells including the PVD neuron, we observed irregularly spaced puncta of PTRN-1a::tdTomato throughout the PVD dendrites and axon (Figure 1B,C, Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Continuous PTRN-1::tdTomato fluorescence was often observed in the primary dendrite adjacent to the cell body.
source: We often observed continuous PTRN-1::tdTomato fluorescence in the primary dendrite adjacent to the cell body, and fewer, farther spaced puncta in the quaternary processes (Figure 1B and data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PTRN-1a puncta colocalized with EMTB::GFP cytosolic threads within the muscle cytosol.
source: The PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta within the muscle cytosol always co-localized with the EMTB::GFP cytosolic threads (Figure 1F), confirming that PTRN-1 localizes to MTs.
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: PTRN-1a puncta colocalized with EMTB::GFP puncta at the sarcolemma.
source: Further, PTRN-1a puncta colocalized with EMTB::GFP puncta at the sarcolemma (Figure 1E), a finding which suggests that, like its homologs in fruitflies and humans (Meng et al., 2008; Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Tanaka et al., 2012), PTRN-1a localizes to MT ends.
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 1E and citations to studies on CAMSAP homologs (Meng et al., 2008; Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Tanaka et al., 2012).

claim: PTRN-1a localizes to MT ends.
source: Further, PTRN-1a puncta colocalized with EMTB::GFP puncta at the sarcolemma (Figure 1E), a finding which suggests that, like its homologs in fruitflies and humans (Meng et al., 2008; Goodwin and Vale, 2010; Tanaka et al., 2012), PTRN-1a localizes to MT ends.
evidence: The claim is inferred from colocalization data and comparison to homologs that bind MT ends.

claim: Highly expressed PTRN-1a::tdTomato localized along the side of MTs in the body wall muscle cells.
source: Although CAMSAP proteins preferentially bind to the minus ends of MTs, when they are overexpressed, CAMSAPs have also been shown to bind along the side of MTs (Meng et al., 2008; Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010). Similarly, highly expressed PTRN-1a::tdTomato localized along the side of MTs in the body wall muscle cells (Figure 1F (bottom left of main panel), Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 5, and citations to studies on CAMSAP overexpression (Meng et al., 2008; Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010).

claim: Acute colchicine treatment dramatically altered the distribution of EMTB::GFP such that fibers were no longer visible.
source: Acute colchicine treatment dramatically altered the distribution of EMTB::GFP such that fibers were no longer visible. Small EMTB::GFP foci remained at the cell membrane and in the cell interior, along with a haze of fluorescence throughout the cytosol (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Colchicine treatment led to MT depolymerization.
source: Since EMTB::GFP normally binds to the sidewalls of MTs (Faire et al., 1999), this change in its distribution confirms that the colchicine treatment led to MT depolymerization, as expected.
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from EMTB::GFP distribution changes and citation to EMTB::GFP binding properties (Faire et al., 1999).

claim: The localization of PTRN-1a::tdTomato appeared to be unaffected by acute colchicine exposure.
source: The localization of PTRN-1a::tdTomato appeared to be unaffected by the acute colchicine exposure, and the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta co-localized with the EMTB::GFP puncta both at the sarcolemma and in the cell interior (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta co-localized with EMTB::GFP puncta both at the sarcolemma and in the cell interior after acute colchicine exposure.
source: The localization of PTRN-1a::tdTomato appeared to be unaffected by the acute colchicine exposure, and the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta co-localized with the EMTB::GFP puncta both at the sarcolemma and in the cell interior (Figure 2A–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: PTRN-1a localization in the body wall muscle cells is not dependent on MTs.
source: These data show that, in the body wall muscle cells, the localization of PTRN-1a puncta is not dependent on MTs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that PTRN-1a localization is unaffected by MT depolymerization.

claim: PTRN-1a localizes to sites where MTs are stabilized, even under conditions that cause complete depolymerization of all other MTs in the cell.
source: They further imply that PTRN-1a localizes to sites where MTs are stabilized, even under conditions that cause complete depolymerization of all other MTs in the cell.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the colocalization of PTRN-1a with remaining EMTB::GFP puncta after colchicine treatment.

claim: In the PVD neuron, acute colchicine exposure caused the continuous EMTB::GFP staining to dissolve into closely spaced puncta.
source: In the PVD neuron, acute colchicine exposure caused the continuous EMTB::GFP staining to dissolve into closely spaced puncta (Figure 2G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2G,H.

claim: The PTRN-1a::tdTomato localization in the PVD neurites appeared unaffected by MT depolymerization.
source: As in the body wall muscle cells, the PTRN-1a::tdTomato localization in the PVD neurites appeared unaffected by the MT depolymerization, and the remaining EMTB::GFP colocalized with the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta (Figure 2G,H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2G,H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The remaining EMTB::GFP colocalized with the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta in PVD neurites after colchicine treatment.
source: As in the body wall muscle cells, the PTRN-1a::tdTomato localization in the PVD neurites appeared unaffected by the MT depolymerization, and the remaining EMTB::GFP colocalized with the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta (Figure 2G,H, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 2G,H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: PTRN-1a localizes to sites where MTs are stabilized in the neurites.
source: We interpret these data as suggestive that PTRN-1a localizes to sites where MTs are stabilized in the neurites.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the colocalization of PTRN-1a with remaining EMTB::GFP puncta after colchicine treatment in neurites.

claim: The CKK domain of CAMSAP proteins is involved in MT binding.
source: As previous studies have shown that the CKK domain of CAMSAP proteins is involved in MT binding (Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010), we analyzed PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato to determine whether PTRN-1a itself stabilizes MTs.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Baines et al., 2009; Goodwin and Vale, 2010).

claim: PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato exhibited similar localization in body wall muscle cells as full-length PTRN-1a::tdTomato.
source: PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato exhibited similar localization in body wall muscle cells as full-length PTRN-1a::tdTomato, though these PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato puncta sometimes did not colocalize with EMTB::GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: After acute colchicine treatment, EMTB::GFP puncta did not colocalize with PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato in body wall muscle cells.
source: Performing acute colchicine treatment on animals co-expressing EMTB::GFP and PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato in the body wall muscle cells, we found that GFP-stained MT filaments were transformed into GFP puncta, but these puncta did not colocalize with PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato (Figure 2E,F, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 2E,F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato localized to puncta in the PVD processes.
source: Finally, although PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato localized to puncta in the PVD processes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C), after acute colchicine exposure, PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato puncta exhibited reduced colocalization with EMTB::GFP (Figure 2I, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: After acute colchicine exposure, PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato puncta exhibited reduced colocalization with EMTB::GFP in PVD processes.
source: Finally, although PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato localized to puncta in the PVD processes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C), after acute colchicine exposure, PTRN-1a(ΔCKK)::tdTomato puncta exhibited reduced colocalization with EMTB::GFP (Figure 2I, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by colocalization data shown in Figure 2I and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: One of the MT ends is more stable than the rest of the MT in vivo, possibly due to end-binding proteins.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that one of the MT ends is more stable than the rest of the MT in vivo, possibly due to end-binding proteins, and PTRN-1a::tdTomato itself stabilizes MT foci.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that MT ends remain after colchicine treatment while the rest of the MT depolymerizes.

claim: PTRN-1a::tdTomato itself stabilizes MT foci.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that one of the MT ends is more stable than the rest of the MT in vivo, possibly due to end-binding proteins, and PTRN-1a::tdTomato itself stabilizes MT foci.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison between full-length PTRN-1a and PTRN-1a(ΔCKK) in colchicine experiments.

claim: Each EBP-2::GFP punctum appeared, migrated in a single direction, and disappeared.
source: As reported for other neurons, each EBP-2::GFP punctum appeared, migrated in a single direction, and disappeared (blue arrowheads, Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,E.

claim: Multiple EBP-2::GFP movements emanated from the same position in some cases.
source: In some cases, multiple EBP-2::GFP movements emanated from the same position in the course of a video, suggestive of a local factor that promotes MT polymerization from these loci.
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data and inference about MT polymerization sites.

claim: PTRN-1a::tdTomato was localized almost exclusively to immobile puncta for the duration of 110 s videos.
source: PTRN-1a::tdTomato, in contrast, was localized almost exclusively to immobile puncta for the duration of these 110 s videos (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,G.

claim: Many of the EBP-2::GFP movements appeared to emanate from PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta.
source: Many of the EBP-2::GFP movements appeared to emanate from PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta, though the close spacing of the PTRN-1a::tdTomato puncta makes quantification of this observation impracticable (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,H.

claim: Strains carrying either of the ptrn-1(null) alleles exhibited grossly wild-type growth, development, and neuronal morphology.
source: Strains carrying either of the ptrn-1(null) alleles exhibited grossly wild-type growth, development, and neuronal morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In wild-type animals, EBP-2::GFP comets move predominantly toward the cell body in the PHC dendrite.
source: In wild-type animals, EBP-2::GFP comets move predominantly toward the cell body (Yan et al., 2013), consistent with the known minus-end-out polarity of MTs in dendrites (Burton, 1985).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Yan et al., 2013; Burton, 1985).

claim: In both ptrn-1 mutant strains, fewer total EBP-2::GFP movements were observed than in the wild-type strain.
source: In both of the ptrn-1 mutant strains, we observed fewer total EBP-2::GFP movements than in the wild-type strain (Figure 4B), but the direction of EBP-2::GFP movements was like that of wild-type (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of EBP-2::GFP movements shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The direction of EBP-2::GFP movements in ptrn-1 mutants was like that of wild-type.
source: In both of the ptrn-1 mutant strains, we observed fewer total EBP-2::GFP movements than in the wild-type strain (Figure 4B), but the direction of EBP-2::GFP movements was like that of wild-type (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of EBP-2::GFP movement direction shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of ptrn-1a::tdTomato in the PHC neuron of ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant animals rescued the decreased number of EBP-2::GFP movements.
source: Expression of ptrn-1a::tdTomato in the PHC neuron of ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant animals rescued the decreased number of EBP-2::GFP movements (Figure 4B), indicating that the requirement for PTRN-1 in promoting EBP-2::GFP movements is cell-autonomous.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The requirement for PTRN-1 in promoting EBP-2::GFP movements is cell-autonomous.
source: Expression of ptrn-1a::tdTomato in the PHC neuron of ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant animals rescued the decreased number of EBP-2::GFP movements (Figure 4B), indicating that the requirement for PTRN-1 in promoting EBP-2::GFP movements is cell-autonomous.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the rescue experiment showing cell-specific expression restores the phenotype.

claim: PTRN-1 is implicated in promoting MT polymerization in the dendrite but not directly organizing MT polarity.
source: These data implicate PTRN-1 in promoting MT polymerization in the dendrite but not directly organizing MT polarity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that ptrn-1 mutants have fewer EBP-2::GFP movements but normal directionality.

claim: Growth in a low dose of colchicine caused dramatic ectopic sprouting from the sides of neurites in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant but not wild-type animals.
source: Although the neurite morphology of many C. elegans neurons in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant all appeared grossly wild-type under normal growth conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), growth in a low dose of colchicine caused dramatic ectopic sprouting from the sides of neurites in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant but not wild-type animals (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant grown in colchicine, ectopic branching of the commissures and additional neurites sprouting from processes in the VNC were observed in DD/VD-type motorneurons.
source: In the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant grown in colchicine, in contrast, we observed ectopic branching of the commissures, as well as additional neurites sprouting from processes in the VNC (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Ectopic branching in ptrn-1 mutants grown in colchicine could be rescued by tissue-specific ptrn-1 expression either pan-neuronally or exclusively in the DD/VD neurons.
source: This ectopic branching could be rescued by tissue-specific ptrn-1 expression either pan-neuronally or exclusively in the DD/VD neurons (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The synthetic interaction between colchicine and ptrn-1 is suggestive that ptrn-1 promotes MT stabilization in the DD/VD-type neurons.
source: This synthetic interaction between colchicine and ptrn-1 is suggestive that ptrn-1 promotes MT stabilization in the DD/VD-type neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the pharmacogenetic interaction between colchicine and ptrn-1.

claim: MT destabilization has long been known to negatively regulate tubulin production.
source: MT destabilization has long been known to negatively regulate tubulin production (Cleveland, 1988).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Cleveland, 1988).

claim: In the C. elegans TRNs, MT destabilization induced by genetic or pharmacological manipulations results in decreased levels β-tubulin mec-7 mRNA and a general decrease in protein production, including GFP driven by the mec-7 promoter.
source: In the C. elegans TRNs, MT destabilization induced by genetic or pharmacological manipulations results in not only decreased levels β-tubulin mec-7 mRNA but also a general decrease in protein production, including GFP driven by the mec-7 promoter (Savage et al., 1994; Bounoutas et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Savage et al., 1994; Bounoutas et al., 2011).

claim: The ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant exhibited decreased GFP fluorescence from a Pmec-7::gfp transgene relative to the wild-type strain.
source: Similarly, the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant exhibited decreased GFP fluorescence from a Pmec-7::gfp transgene relative to the wild-type strain (Figure 5I), further implicating PTRN-1 in promoting MT stability.
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence quantification data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Decreased GFP fluorescence from a Pmec-7::gfp transgene in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant further implicates PTRN-1 in promoting MT stability.
source: Similarly, the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant exhibited decreased GFP fluorescence from a Pmec-7::gfp transgene relative to the wild-type strain (Figure 5I), further implicating PTRN-1 in promoting MT stability.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the known relationship between MT stability and mec-7 promoter activity.

claim: Cross sections of the PLML/R axons from two ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant young adult animals had 13, 15, 2, and 14 MTs, respectively.
source: We examined cross sections of the PLML/R axons from two ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant young adult animals sectioned at the rectum and found they had 13, 15, 2, and 14 MTs, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data.

claim: In wild-type animals reared at 25°C, there are 25–50 15-pf MTs and occasionally one or two 11-pf MTs in cross sections of the PLM neuron.
source: In cross sections of the PLM neuron in wild-type animals reared at 25°C, there are 25–50 15-pf MTs and occasionally one or two 11-pf MTs (Figure 5J) (Chalfie and Thomson, 1979; Cueva et al., 2012; our unpublished data).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5J and citations to previous studies (Chalfie and Thomson, 1979; Cueva et al., 2012).

claim: In ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant PLM neurons, several MTs had smaller diameters indicative of 11-pf MTs.
source: The majority of these MTs had the characteristically large diameter of 15-pf MTs, but several MTs had smaller diameters indicative of 11-pf MTs (Figure 5K).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: In one of the PLML cross sections from ptrn-1(tm5597) mutants, an irregular MT structure that was 'S' shaped instead of circular was observed.
source: Furthermore, in one of the PLML cross sections, we observed an irregular MT structure that persisted through three serial sections (150 nm) that was 'S' shaped instead of circular (Figure 5K).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5K.

claim: The reduction in MT number found in all four cells, as well as the 'S' shaped MT structure in one, implicates a role for PTRN-1 in maintaining the integrity of MTs in neuronal processes.
source: The reduction in MT number found in all four cells, as well as the 'S' shaped MT structure in one, implicates a role for PTRN-1 in maintaining the integrity of MTs in neuronal processes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the electron microscopy observations of reduced MT number and abnormal MT structure.

claim: Roughly 20% of ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant L4 animals exhibited defective extension of the PLM commissure.
source: Roughly 20% of ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant L4 animals exhibited defective extension of the PLM commissure (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 6A–C.

claim: In wild-type animals, the PLM commissure is extended during the L1 larval stage from the axon to the VNC posterior of and close to the vulva, and it is present in every L4 animal.
source: In wild-type animals, this commissure is extended during the L1 larval stage from the axon to the VNC posterior of and close to the vulva, and it is present in every L4 animal (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by morphological data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The defective PLM commissure extension observed in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant was fully rescued by ptrn-1a cDNA expressed in the PLM neuron.
source: The defective PLM commissure extension observed in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant was fully rescued by ptrn-1a cDNA expressed in the PLM neuron, indicating that the role for PTRN-1 in commissure formation is cell-autonomous (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The role for PTRN-1 in commissure formation is cell-autonomous.
source: The defective PLM commissure extension observed in the ptrn-1(tm5597) mutant was fully rescued by ptrn-1a cDNA expressed in the PLM neuron, indicating that the role for PTRN-1 in commissure formation is cell-autonomous (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cell-specific rescue experiment.

claim: In wild-type animals, mCherry::RAB-3 localized to two patches along the VNC that correspond to the synaptic patches of the two PLM neurons.
source: In wild-type animals, mCherry::RAB-3 localized to two patches along the VNC that correspond to the synaptic patches of the two PLM neurons (Figure 6D,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6D,H.

claim: In the ptrn-1 mutants, there was an incompletely penetrant loss of mCherry::RAB-3 at the synaptic patch region.
source: In the ptrn-1 mutants, there was an incompletely penetrant loss of mCherry::RAB-3 at the synaptic patch region, and in many ptrn-1 mutant animals, at least one of the PLM neurons had no visible accumulation of mCherry::RAB-3 at the synaptic patch (Figure 6E,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6E,H.

claim: The ptrn-1(wy560) strain had a higher penetrance of loss of mCherry::RAB-3 at the synaptic patch than the ptrn-1(tm5597) strain.
source: The ptrn-1(wy560) strain had a higher penetrance of this defect than the ptrn-1(tm5597) strain (Figure 6H).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: The ptrn-1(wy560) allele is a deletion that removes not only the entire ptrn-1 locus but also seven surrounding ORFs, including the Muscleblind homolog mbl-1.
source: The ptrn-1(wy560) allele is a deletion that removes not only the entire ptrn-1 locus but also seven surrounding ORFs, including the Muscleblind homolog mbl-1.
evidence: The claim is supported by genetic characterization of the allele.

claim: mbl-1 has been shown to promote the accumulation of synaptic material at the presynaptic region of other C. elegans neurons.
source: As mbl-1 has been shown to promote the accumulation of synaptic material at the presynaptic region of other C. elegans neurons (Spilker et al., 2012), we speculate that this difference in penetrance might be due to mbl-1 deficiency in the wy560 allele.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Spilker et al., 2012).

claim: The difference in penetrance between ptrn-1(wy560) and ptrn-1(tm5597) might be due to mbl-1 deficiency in the wy560 allele.
source: As mbl-1 has been shown to promote the accumulation of synaptic material at the presynaptic region of other C. elegans neurons (Spilker et al., 2012), we speculate that this difference in penetrance might be due to mbl-1 deficiency in the wy560 allele.
evidence: The claim is speculative inference based on the known function of mbl-1.

claim: A fully penetrant ectopic accumulation of mCherry::RAB-3 in the PLM posterior process was observed in both ptrn-1 mutant strains.
source: In addition to the loss of mCherry::RAB-3 from the synaptic patches, we observed a fully penetrant ectopic accumulation of mCherry::RAB-3 in the PLM posterior process in both ptrn-1 mutant strains (Figure 6F–H).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6F–H.

claim: The localization of SNB-1::GFP in the PLM neuron of ptrn-1(tm5597) was similar to that of RAB-3::mCherry.
source: The localization of SNB-1::GFP in the PLM neuron of ptrn-1(tm5597) was similar to that of RAB-3::mCherry (Figure 6I).
evidence: The claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Two different promoters driving ptrn-1a::yfp cDNA expression in the PLM neuron of the ptrn-1 mutants rescued the defects in mCherry::RAB-3 localization.
source: To determine whether the requirement for ptrn-1 in SV localization is cell-autonomous, we used two different promoters to drive ptrn-1a::yfp cDNA expression in the PLM neuron of the ptrn-1 mutants. Both constructs rescued the defects in mCherry::RAB-3 localization (Figure 6H), indicating that PTRN-1 functions cell autonomously in the PLM neuron to promote proper SV localization.
evidence: The claim is supported by rescue experiment data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: PTRN-1 functions cell autonomously in the PLM neuron to promote proper SV localization.
source: To determine whether the requirement for ptrn-1 in SV localization is cell-autonomous, we used two different promoters to drive ptrn-1a::yfp cDNA expression in the PLM neuron of the ptrn-1 mutants. Both constructs rescued the defects in mCherry::RAB-3 localization (Figure 6H), indicating that PTRN-1 functions cell autonomously in the PLM neuron to promote proper SV localization.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cell-specific rescue experiment.

claim: DLK-1 is a conserved mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase (MAPKKK) that functions in a variety of situations in neurons, including neurite outgrowth, synapse development, and axon regeneration.
source: DLK-1 is a conserved mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase (MAPKKK) that functions in a variety of situations in neurons, including neurite outgrowth, synapse development, and axon regeneration (Tedeschi and Bradke, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a review (Tedeschi and Bradke, 2013).

claim: In C. elegans, the DLK-1 pathway is required to mediate the response to MT destabilization in the PLM neuron, and it also promotes proper synapse localization.
